note: A fictional teaching document. Every value in it was invented for this index; no supplier, laboratory, batch or result here corresponds to anything real, and none was copied from a real certificate. It exists so that a reader can be shown where the useful questions sit on a page of this shape, and it is deliberately imperfect: the omissions are the lesson.
documentTitle: SPECIMEN — Analytical Test Report (fictional teaching document)
laboratoryAddress: Unit 0, Example Industrial Estate, Exampleton (fictional address)
provenanceNotes: Constructed for this index as a teaching document. Not received from any supplier and not based on any real certificate.
statedStrength: Labelled 10 mg per vial (label claim, not a measured result)
whatItDemonstrates: That a named laboratory reports having performed the listed tests on a sample it received, obtaining the results shown, on the stated dates.
whatItDoesNotDemonstrate: Who manufactured the material; whether the sample the laboratory received was drawn from the batch named, or was representative of it; whether the material in any particular container is that batch; and whether any result is correct, since nothing here has been checked against anything but this document; and how much peptide the vial contains, which no test on this report measures despite the label stating an amount.
provenanceGaps: The document names no original manufacturer, so the material's origin cannot be traced from it. The sample was submitted by the reseller rather than drawn under any custody arrangement described here, so the link between the batch named and the material tested rests entirely on the submitter's assertion.
missingFields: Whether the tested material was an API, bulk material or finished product
Method reference for the water determination
How the sample was drawn and by whom
Any determination of peptide content, against a stated label claim of 10 mg
Acceptance criterion for the identity result
unverifiedRelationships: Batch EXB-0000 to the submitted sample; the reseller to any manufacturer; this report to any container a reader might hold.

tests.analyticalMethod: Reversed-phase HPLC, UV detection at 214 nm
tests.specificationText: Not less than 98.0% (as stated by the submitter)
tests.attachmentReference: Chromatogram referenced as Annex 1 (not supplied with this specimen)
tests.teachingNote: The figure most readers stop at. It describes how mixed the submitted sample was under one set of conditions — not what the material is, how much of it there is, or whether it came from the batch named. Note also that the acceptance criterion here was supplied by the party selling the material.

tests.analyticalMethod: Liquid chromatography with mass spectrometric detection
tests.resultText: Observed mass consistent with the expected monoisotopic mass
tests.teachingNote: No acceptance criterion is stated, so 'consistent with' is the laboratory's judgement rather than a measurement against a limit. A mass result bears on identity; the purity figure above does not.

The vial is labelled 10 mg and this report does not measure how much peptide is present. A label is a claim by whoever wrote it; a content result would be a measurement made on a sample by a named method. The purity figure above does not supply the missing number — it describes proportions among what was detected, not a quantity.
A number with no stated limit. Whether 6.4% is acceptable depends on a specification this document does not carry, and this index holds no source stating one.
Listed precisely because it was not performed. A certificate covering purity and identity is silent about sterility, and silence is easy to read as reassurance.
